title: Emissions gap

definition.text: The difference between the emission cuts countries have pledged and the cuts needed to meet a temperature goal, tracked in UNEP's annual Emissions Gap Report.

facts.text: UNEP first assessed in November 2010 a gap between Copenhagen Accord pledges and the cuts needed for a likely chance of meeting 2 °C.
The 2022 Emissions Gap Report said emissions needed to be almost halved.
The 2024 report found current policies would likely lead to 3.1 °C of warming, and full pledges to 1.9 °C.
The 2020 report said 1.5 °C needs a 57% global cut from 2019 levels by 2030.

notes: Phrase concept; mentioned on several in-scope pages (Climate change mitigation, Greenhouse gas, Greenhouse gas emissions, Copenhagen climate summit, Solar radiation modification).
